title: Ramayana Part 2 Will Arrive in 2028, Producer Namit Malhotra Confirms
excerpt: On the eve of Part 1 release on November 5, producer Namit Malhotra has confirmed the sequel moves from its planned Diwali 2027 window to 2028, saying the finale needs the extra year. The Hindi film is also being made in a separate English master version.
body:
• Ramayana: Part 2 will not release in 2027. Producer Namit Malhotra has confirmed the second part of the two-part epic will arrive in 2028, a year later than the Diwali 2027 window originally planned.
  • Part 1 — a Hindi film, also prepared in a separate English master version with a different edit and runtime — releases in theatres on Thursday, November 5, ahead of Diwali.
  • Malhotra reason, in his own words: the team needed the extra year to do justice to a film of this size, and did not want a rush job on the finale, which carries the war between Rama and Ravana. Shooting for Part 2 is still pending and resumes next month.
  • The film was first planned as a trilogy, then settled as two parts; Malhotra says the team may revisit the structure after seeing how the world receives Part 1.

The wait between the two halves of Indian cinema biggest production just doubled. Producer Namit Malhotra has made it official that Ramayana: Part 2 is not releasing in 2027, confirming reports that the sequel will arrive in 2028 instead, according to Telugu360. The announcement comes a day before Part 1 opens in theatres on November 5.

"That extra year is what I genuinely believe we need to do justice for a film of this size. When you see part 2 coming in, that will be a whole other story. We didn’t want to do a rush job or get ahead of ourselves."

— Namit Malhotra, producer, in an interview with E! News reported by Bollywood Bubble

Why the sequel needs the time

Part 2 carries the epic centrepiece: the war between Rama and Ravana. Malhotra said the shoot of the second part is still pending and will resume next month, and that the team is not ready to compromise on quality, according to Telugu360. There is also a second production running in parallel: the filmmakers have created two master versions of the film, with the English version given a different edit and a rewritten script rather than a straight translation, Bollywood Bubble reported from the same interview. Malhotra admitted he would love not to have to make two versions — and that director Nitesh Tiwari would prefer one cut as well.

The film, and what came before

Ramayana is Nitesh Tiwari two-part retelling of the epic, produced by Malhotra and Yash on a reported budget of Rs 4,000 crore. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Yash plays Ravana, Ravie Dubey plays Lakshman and Sunny Deol plays Lord Hanuman. The project was initially planned as a trilogy before the makers settled on two parts — and that question is not fully closed. Malhotra said the team may sit back after Part 1 and reconsider whether to add or subtract, depending on how the world receives it, according to Bollywood Bubble; Hauterrfly carried the same confirmation, citing Hindustan Times reporting.

What this means for viewers

For audiences, the practical facts are simple. Part 1 opens Thursday, November 5, in Hindi and in an English version, in theatres worldwide including the United States. Anyone who watches it this weekend is now committing to a two-year wait for the conclusion — the originally announced one-year gap to Diwali 2027 is gone, and no exact 2028 date has been announced. Whether the gap hurts the second film momentum will be the industry question of 2027; the makers are betting that a better finale is worth more than a faster one.
